Privacy Policy

Last updated: November 20, 2026

Meowshift (“the App”) cares about your personal data and work data. This policy explains how the App handles data when providing scheduling, pay estimates, cloud sync, subscriptions and PRO smart tools.

1. Data on your device

Schedules, pay settings, leave records and some personalization settings are stored on your device first. Unless PRO cloud sync is turned on, this work data is not uploaded just because you sign in.

2. Account sign-in

You can create or sign in to an account in the App with a supported third-party sign-in service. The sign-in service may give the App the account identifiers it needs, such as a user ID, display name or account information provided by that service. What is actually shared depends on the sign-in service and the scope you authorize.

If you buy PRO in the App without signing in, the App creates an anonymous account for this phone the moment you tap buy, with no name or email address, to tie the purchase to your PRO access. Your work data stays only on this device; cloud sync and cloud backup turn on only after you link Google, LINE or Apple in Me › Account.

3. PRO cloud sync

Only when you have an active PRO plan (including the first 7 days of full PRO for a new account) and have turned on cloud sync yourself does the App send your workspace data to Supabase, to provide backups, sync across devices and data restore. During the 7 days of full PRO, uploading starts only after you tap “Turn on cloud backup” on the Cloud sync page. You can turn off cloud sync in the App.

After PRO ends, the cloud is no longer updated, but when you sign in to the same account you can still load and restore the data you left in the cloud earlier; to delete the cloud data, you can permanently delete your account.

Depending on what you enter and which features you turn on, the cloud workspace may include: schedules, working hours, leave types and notes, health-related leave records such as sick or menstrual leave, financial information such as pay and deductions, your username, profile photo, shift swap and cover records (including the names you enter for coworkers), income threshold alert settings and other personalization settings. Cash balances you enter in the Payday calendar are kept only on this device and are never uploaded.

Shared schedules Shared schedules need a signed-in account. The people you share with can see the name you chose and your schedule from yesterday to about 3 months ahead: which days you work, shift names with start and end times, and the jobs you tick. Overtime end times, and whether a leave day shows as a day off, shows the leave type or is hidden, follow your choice for each person. Pay, amounts and notes are never uploaded, and the other person never sees them. This data is kept on the Supabase server the App uses (Tokyo, Japan) and only the people you share with can see it; an invite code works for 7 days and only once. When you stop sharing, the other person stops seeing your schedule right away; once you share with no one and have no invite code that can still be used, the schedule you uploaded is deleted from the server, and it is also deleted when you delete your account.

Your Cat nest game record (best score and number of plays) is synced together with your work data.

4. Subscriptions and payments

PRO subscriptions on iOS are handled by the Apple App Store, and on Android by Google Play. The App receives and keeps the transaction and entitlement status needed to provide your subscription, such as the plan, status, expiry time and store transaction identifiers. Payment credentials such as card numbers are handled by Apple or Google Play; the App never receives your full card details.

7 days of full PRO New accounts (and accounts signing in for the first time on this version) can use PRO features at no cost for their first 7 days, with no payment and no auto-renewal. So that each person can use this only once, the App’s servers keep the time the 7 days started for each account, and also keep a non-reversible hash (SHA-256), computed from the sign-in service (Apple, Google or LINE) and the account identifier that service provides, together with the start time. This hash contains no name, email address or original account identifier and cannot be turned back into them; it is used only to tell whether the same sign-in account has already used its 7 days. It is kept even after the account is deleted, so the 7 days can’t be claimed again by deleting the account and signing up again.

After PRO’s auto-renewal is turned off or PRO has ended, the App may ask you why, which you can skip; the reasons and note you send are kept on the App’s servers with the App version, language and country code, used only to improve the App, do not affect your subscription, and are deleted when you delete your account.

5. Smart tools and payslip cross-check

Meow Assistant voice input When you tap the microphone, the App uses your phone's built-in speech recognition to turn your speech into a text command: the iOS version uses Apple's speech recognition, and the Android version uses the phone's built-in speech recognition service (provided by Google on most phones). Your speech may be processed on your device or by that service's servers. The App does not record audio and does not send your speech to the App's servers. The microphone is not used for this feature when you're not using voice input.

Meow Assistant chat When a PRO user (including during the first 7 days of full PRO) talks to Meow Assistant, the text you type or say, your last few messages, and the work data the answer needs (for example your schedule for the weeks before and after, this month’s overtime and estimated pay, annual leave, hire date, and job and shift names) are sent through a protected backend service to a third-party AI service to write the reply. When up-to-date information is needed, the third-party AI service may search the web for public information based on your question (for labor laws, only official government websites), and the answer shows its sources. When a web search is needed, only your question and the last few things you said, today’s date, the labor-rule region that applies and the App language are sent for the search; your schedule, pay, job and shift names, hire date and similar data are not attached. The App’s servers only record how many times and how much you use it each day, and do not keep the content of your chats. Your chat history is stored only on this device, up to 50 messages, and you can delete it in Meow Assistant under “⋯ → Clear chat”. AI answers may be wrong; for legal, medical or money matters, rely on announcements from the competent authorities or on professionals.

Payslip recognition The PRO payslip feature cross-checks using multiple recognition passes, semantic analysis and pay rules. To do this, one processed payslip image and the necessary recognized text may be sent through a protected backend service to a third-party AI service for analysis. If readings disagree or confidence is low, the App flags the fields concerned for you to confirm and never overwrites your data with uncertain results.

Image storage The App doesn't save payslip images to its work-data cloud or general file storage. Requests sent to third-party AI services use settings that don't create application-level content storage; those services may still process necessary service logs under their own data-processing and security policies.

Line-by-line pay check Once a payslip is recognized, the App re-checks amount differences against your schedule, pay settings and the payslip itself. Any additions or deductions on the payslip that the estimate didn't include are listed separately for you to confirm.

6. Notifications

On iOS and Android, reminders and shift alarms use local notifications on your device, and their scheduling is managed by the device's system. On iOS, the real alarm (iOS 26 or later) and the PRO Lock Screen countdown are likewise scheduled and shown on your device by its system. The first time you set a reminder, the App asks for notification permission as the system requires, and it asks for alarm permission when you turn on the real alarm; you can turn these off in iOS or Android system settings.

Update & event notifications When you have allowed notifications and are signed in, the App stores this phone’s push token, the App language and version, and the notification switch on the App’s servers, only to send App update and event notifications. You can turn this off under “Me › Notifications”, and it is deleted when you delete your account.

Usage statistics The first time the App is opened each day, it sends a randomly generated install ID that isn't linked to your account, along with the platform, app version, language, country code, phone model and system version, used only to count how many people use the App each day and which phones and system versions they use. It doesn't include your name, account, phone name or any work data.

Plan page statistics When you open the Plan page, tap subscribe, or complete or cancel a payment in the store, the App sends the same install ID with the name of that step, whether you chose monthly or yearly, which PRO feature brought you there, whether your first 7 days of PRO are still running, and the platform, app version, language and country code. It is used only to see where the Plan page needs improving. It contains no name, account, payment details or work data.

Keeping and turning off usage statistics Usage statistics are deleted automatically after 13 months. To stop sending them, turn off “Send anonymous usage statistics” at the bottom of “Me › Privacy Policy”; once off, nothing more is sent.

Crash and error diagnostics To find and fix crashes, the iOS and Android apps send a crash report or the error details to a third-party error-monitoring service when the App crashes, stops responding or hits a program error, together with the phone model, system version, App version and a random number that belongs only to this installation. Each time the App opens it also sends a record with no content, used to work out the share of sessions without a crash. This data contains no name, email address, account, or work data such as your schedule or pay, and none of the text you type, what you tap or screenshots; web addresses keep only their path, without query details. It is used only to fix problems, never for advertising or tracking, and is not linked to your account.

7. Data retention and deletion

You can choose “Delete account permanently” under “Me → Account”. Once the account is deleted, the cloud work data, entitlement data and other data directly linked to it are deleted; transaction event records required by law, accounting, fraud prevention or store transaction audits may be kept in a form unlinked from you. To prevent the first 7 days of full PRO from being claimed again, the server keeps the non-reversible sign-in hash and start time described above; they contain no personally identifiable data and are not linked to any work data. The local workspace, the Meow Assistant chat history and the PRO monthly recap on your device are also cleared.

Deleting your App account doesn't automatically cancel a store auto-renewal. If you have an active subscription, cancel renewal through Apple's “Subscriptions” on iOS, or Google Play's “Payments & subscriptions” on Android.

8. Third-party services

The App may currently use third-party services such as Apple, Supabase, Google, LINE and Meta to provide payments, authentication, cloud sync, speech recognition, AI features for schedules, payslips and Meow Assistant, sign-in, and opening the App from Meta ad links. Each of these services handles data under its own privacy policy and data-processing terms.

Ad measurement (iOS): The iOS App uses App Events from the Meta (Facebook) SDK to record app installs, app launches and App Store purchases, to measure how Meta ads perform. The App doesn't ask for App Tracking Transparency permission and doesn't collect the advertising identifier (IDFA); extra metadata such as screen titles and app links is turned off. Your schedules, pay, health-related leave, events and other work data are never sent to Meta.

Error monitoring The App also uses a third-party error-monitoring service to receive crash and error diagnostics (see section 6), only to fix problems in the App; this service receives no account or work data.

9. App Store privacy disclosure summary

The App doesn't use your data for advertising tracking across other companies. Depending on the features you actually use, the App Store privacy disclosure may include: name, email address, user ID, purchase history, other financial info, health-related data, photos or videos, other user content and device ID (push token), used for App functionality and account / cloud services. There are also usage statistics not linked to your identity (device ID, product interaction, other diagnostic data), used only for analytics.

In addition, crash data, performance data and other diagnostic data, not linked to your identity, are used only to fix problems in the App.

10. Data security

The App takes reasonable technical and access-control measures, including account authentication, Row Level Security, separated backend permissions and transferring only the data needed. However, no electronic system can be guaranteed 100% secure.

11. Policy updates and contact

This policy may be updated as features, laws or third-party services change. The latest version is posted on this page. To contact the developer, use the App's “Contact support” page or the developer contact details on the App Store product page.
